result.topic_en: Second page of a letter from G. H. Hardy (apparently to G. N. Watson) about sending Ramanujan manuscripts obtained from Miss S, listing contents including the suppressed part of 'Highly Composite Numbers', with a postscript about a pupil working on the asymptotics of coefficients of $1/((1-ax)(1-ax^2)\cdots)$.
result.transcription:
(2)
be wise to send to you at once —
by now, you can probably 'place' most
of them.
Of course, I have a good many
more which need sorting out.
Contents:
3 connected blocks (the most
important being the suppressed part
of 'H.C.N') These Miss S has
attached slips to
block of misc. stuff[?] : I have noted
in pencil the sort of field of
his work they hang on to
You may expect some more after
my further interview with her
Yours
GHHardy

N.B. I have a pupil working (inter alia)
at $\sum c_n x^n = \frac{1}{(1-ax)(1-ax^2)\cdots}$ , $c_n \sim \sqrt{1-a}\,\frac{(kn)^{\frac14}}{2n\sqrt{\pi}}\,e^{2\sqrt{kn}}$
— so don't queer his pitch!

[margin, another hand:] Highly Composite Numbers
Collected Papers, p. 78

methods.what: Asymptotic formula for coefficients of the generating function $1/\prod_{m\ge1}(1-ax^m)$

items.english: The coefficients $c_n$ of $1/((1-ax)(1-ax^2)\cdots)$ are asymptotic to $\sqrt{1-a}\,(kn)^{1/4} e^{2\sqrt{kn}}/(2n\sqrt{\pi})$.

items.quote:
You may expect some more after
my further interview with her
items.english: Hardy expects to send more manuscripts after another meeting with Miss S.
